english.title: Provide information relating to notification requirement known to be false
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being subject to

(A)_[a stalking protection order,]_
(B)_[an interim stalking protection order,]_

notified to the police in purported compliance with section 9 of the Stalking Protection Act 2019 information, namely **(..SPECIFY INFORMATION..) which you knew to be false
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 9, 11(1)(b) and (2) of the Stalking Protection Act 2019.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Persons under 18 can be charged with this offence.
(ii) There is no guidance regarding what amounts to a 'reasonable excuse' for the purpose of the Act.
(iii) This section relates to situations where false information has been provided regarding a persons name and addresses, however the offence can be committed by persons other than the individual who is subject to notification requirements.
(iv) Proceedings for an offence committed under this section may be commenced in any court having jurisdiction in any place where the person charges with the offence resides / found. See section 11(6).

other.penalty:
Either way -Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Note
In relation to an offence committed before section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 comes into force, the reference to 12 months should be read as reference to 6 months imprisonment.
